idiom_name: Play render { case Accepts.Html() / Accepts.Json() } + Twirl templates
implementation_notes: Play parses the Accept header into acceptedTypes and Controller#render takes a partial function from MediaRange to Result, so one action builds the model once and returns Ok(views.html.movie(m)) for the HTML representation or Ok(Json.toJson(m)) for the JSON one, with custom media types declared as Accepting("audio/mp3"). Twirl compiles templates into functions over the model at build time, which is Play's version of the shared logical view, and the extractor list is the view registry. An explicit actor/stream fan-out to several live renderers is only needed outside the HTTP cycle (Pekko streams pushing to an HTML client and a metrics sink).
pitfalls: render answers NotAcceptable (406) when no extractor matches, so a client sending an unexpected media range receives an empty 406 that looks like a server fault.

The action body runs once for all media ranges: side effects such as audit writes or counters placed next to the model stay single, which is intended - but per-representation side effects must live inside the extractor branches.
Json.toJson needs an implicit Writes; sharing one Writes between the HTML context and the API means fields the page needs leak into the JSON unless a separate DTO/Writes is defined.
